# Context

This script provides select code to count behavioral health inpatient and residential facility days covered by Medicare, Medicaid, or both. Behavioral health visit days have a primary diagnosis code for substance use disorder, severe mental illness, or mild-to-moderate mental health diagnoses (as defined in scripts `select_code_to_identify_MH_conditions.Rmd` and `select_code_to_identify_SUD.Rmd`).

To identify inpatient and residential facility days, this code assumes the user has created a combined claims table of Medicare encounters (from the Inpatient files) and TAF claims (from the Inpatient, Long-term, and Other Services file). 

Prior to combining claim sets, users should also exclude TAF crossover claims (crossover_clm_ind == 1) as well as Medicare encounters with procedure code modifiers that indicate a "Medicaid level of care" and were thus not paid for by Medicare, including U1-U9, UA, UB, UC, and UD. See [here](https://www.hcpcsdata.com/Modifiers/U)  

Once claim sets are combined, the claims table (named "claims" below) should include the following columns:  
- bene_id  
- claim_id  
- from_dt (claim header begin date)    
- thru_dt (claim header end date)  
- line_from_dt (either the line date or revenue center from date)
- line_thru_dt (either the line date or revenue center thru date)
- primary diagnosis code  
- revenue center code  
- procedure code (cpt/hcpcs codes)  
- ot_accmdtn_hcpcs_rate (from the TAF Other Services file)
- source file ("taf" or "ma") 
- file type ("ma_ip", "taf_ot", "taf_ip", "taf_lt")



# Load lookup tables

Load the behavioral health code lookup tables and the Milbank code sets

```{r}
# mental health icd codes
mh_codes <- fread("mental_health_icd_codes.csv")

# sud icd codes
load("ccw30_sud_codes.RData")

# behavioral health outpatient cpt codes
bh_cpts <- fread("outpt_bh_cpts.csv")

# Milbank code sets
milbank <- fread("milbank_ip_residential_codes.csv")
```


# Flag and restrict to behavioral health visits

```{r}
# flag each BH condition catgegory
claims[ , `:=` (sud_dx  = icd_dgns_cd1 %in% sud_icd10,
                mmmi_dx = icd_dgns_cd1 %in% mh_codes[condition == "mild_mod_mh", icd10],
                smi_dx  = icd_dgns_cd1 %in% mh_codes[condition == "smi", icd10])] %>%
  .[ , bh_dx := mmmi_dx == T | sud_dx == T | smi_dx == T]

# keep only BH claims 
claims <- claims[bh_dx == T]
```


# Establish Milbank code sets

Milbank code sets were adapted from the [following report](https://www.milbank.org/publications/recommendations-for-a-standardized-state-methodology-to-measure-clinical-behavioral-health-spending/)

```{r}
# inpatient codes
mil_ip_rev <- milbank[grepl("Inpatient", setting) & code_type == "Revenue", code]
mil_ip_pos <- milbank[grepl("Inpatient", setting) & code_type == "POS", code]
mil_ip_cpt <- milbank[grepl("Inpatient", setting) & code_type == "CPT", code]

# residential codes
mil_res_rev <- milbank[grepl("Residential", setting) & code_type == "Revenue", code]
mil_res_pos <- milbank[grepl("Residential", setting) & code_type == "POS", code]
mil_res_cpt <- milbank[grepl("Residential", setting) & code_type == "CPT", code]
```


# Flag IP/Residential claims

IP requires either revenue code or CPT + POS. Residential requires revenue code OR CPT OR POS.  

```{r}
# flag components on claim lines
claims[ , `:=` (ip_rev  = rev_cntr %in% mil_ip_rev,
                ip_poscpt = (hcpcs_cd %in% mil_ip_cpt | ot_accmdtn_hcpcs_rate %in% mil_ip_cpt) & plcsrvc %in% mil_ip_pos, 
                res_rev = rev_cntr %in% mil_res_rev,
                res_cpt = hcpcs_cd %in% mil_res_cpt | ot_accmdtn_hcpcs_rate %in% mil_res_cpt,
                res_pos = plcsrvc  %in% mil_res_pos)] 

# flag IP/Res claim lines
claims[ , `:=` (ip  = ip_rev  == T | ip_poscpt == T, 
                res = res_rev == T | res_cpt   == T | res_pos == T)] 

# roll flag to the claim level
claims[ , c("ip", "res") := lapply(.SD, max), .SDcols = c("ip", "res"), by = .(bene_id, clm_id, source)]
 
# if a claim is both IP and Res, we count it as IP
claims[ip == T & res == T, res := F]
```


# Limit to IP/Res claim lines
  
```{r}
ipres_all <- claims[(ip == T  &  (ip_poscpt == T | ip_rev == T))  |
                    (res == T &  (res_cpt == T | res_pos == T | res_rev == T))]
```

 
# Drop some MA residential claims 

We dropped MA claims that were flagged residential based on place of service alone. It is our understanding that MA doesn't cover residential stays, so if the claim does not also include a valid CPT or revenue center code we drop it here.

```{r}
ipres_all <- ipres_all[!(res == T & res_pos == T & res_cpt == F & res_rev == F & source == "ma")]
```


# Create setting variable
 
```{r}
ipres_all[ , setting := ifelse(ip == T, "ip", "res")]
```


# Identify IP/Residential dates

To identify inpatient and residential days, we use line dates when available and claim header dates when they are not.

```{r}
ipres_all[ , `:=` (start_dt = as.Date(ifelse(!is.na(line_from_dt), line_from_dt, from_dt)),
                   end_dt   = as.Date(ifelse(!is.na(line_thru_dt), line_thru_dt, thru_dt)))]


# some facility claims bill for the entire month as evidenced by the adsmn/disch or header from/thru dates but have a claim line start and end date of the same day. for these we change the end date to the end of the month
ipres_all[file %in% c("taf_ip", "taf_lt") & start_dt == end_dt & mday(start_dt) == 1, 
          end_dt := ceiling_date(end_dt, "month") - 1]

# if there are any cases in which start_dt occurs after end_dt, set start_dt to end_dt
ipres_all[start_dt > end_dt, start_dt := end_dt]
```


# Transform data to one day per row

```{r}
# flag one day claims
ipres_all[ , days := as.numeric(end_dt - start_dt + 1)] %>% .[ , oneday := days == 1]

# separate one day and multi-day claims
ipres_multiday <- ipres_all[oneday == F] %>% .[ , rownum := .I] 
ipres_oneday <- ipres_all[oneday == T]

# expand long so each day is on a separate row
ipres_multiday_expand <- ipres_multiday[, .(date = seq(start_dt, end_dt, by = "day")), by = rownum]

# add back other vars
ipres_multiday_expand <- merge(ipres_multiday_expand, 
                               ipres_multiday,
                               by = "rownum", 
                               all = T)

# set start_dt and end_dt equal to date
ipres_multiday_expand[, `:=`(daystart_dt = date, dayend_dt = date)] %>%
  .[, c("date", "rownum") := NULL]

# rejoin one-day and multi-day claims,  nrow should grow. 
nrow(ipres_all)
ipres_all <- rbind(ipres_oneday[ , `:=` (daystart_dt = start_dt, dayend_dt = end_dt)], 
                   ipres_multiday_expand)
nrow(ipres_all)


# limit to days in study year
ipres_all <- ipres_all[year(daystart_dt) == 2021]

# drop vars
ipres_all[ , c("days", "oneday") := NULL]
rm(ipres_oneday, ipres_multiday, ipres_multiday_expand)
```


# Drop more crossover claims  

Some TAF claims have the same date of service, primary diagnosis code, and procedure code as a Medicare encounter. We consider these "crossover claims" that weren't flagged by crossover_clm_ind == 1. For inpatient crossovers, we exclude the TAF claims from the dataset and attribute the service to Medicare. For residential stay crossovers, we exclude the Medicare claim from the dataset and attribute the service to Medicaid.   

*Note: the res definition includes POS on its own, but we don't check for POS matches because MA and TAF could be paying for different CPTs in the res setting. POS is too vague to consider it a match just based on that.* 

Before checking to see if MA and TAF claims match by procedure code, we need to clean up the TAF OT procedure code, since it can be in one of two different fields (hcpcs_cd or ot_accmdtn_hcpcs_rate). We'll create a unified procedure code variable that pulls the Milbank CPT from whichever field has it. 

```{r}
# if the Milbank CPT code is in the ot_accmdtn_hcpcs_rate field, move that value into hcpcs_cd
ipres_all[(res_cpt == T | ip_poscpt == T) & !hcpcs_cd %in% c(mil_res_cpt, mil_ip_cpt), hcpcs_cd := ot_accmdtn_hcpcs_rate]

ipres_all$ot_accmdtn_hcpcs_rate <- NULL
```


## Drop IP crossover claims

```{r}
# separate MA and TAF, IP and Res
all_ip_ma   <- ipres_all[source == "ma"  & setting == "ip"]
all_ip_taf  <- ipres_all[source == "taf" & setting == "ip"] 
all_res_ma  <- ipres_all[source == "ma"  & setting == "res"]
all_res_taf <- ipres_all[source == "taf" & setting == "res"]

rm(ipres_all)

# merge MA onto TAF by date, diagnosis, and CPT
all_ip_taf <- merge(all_ip_taf,
                    unique(all_ip_ma[!is.na(hcpcs_cd), .(bene_id, daystart_dt, dayend_dt, 
                                                         icd_dgns_cd1, hcpcs_cd, crossover_cpt = T)]),
                    by = c("bene_id", "daystart_dt", "dayend_dt", "icd_dgns_cd1", "hcpcs_cd"), 
                    all.x = T) %>%
  .[is.na(crossover_cpt) , crossover_cpt := F]


# merge MA onto TAF by date, dx and Rev code
all_ip_taf <- merge(all_ip_taf,
                    unique(all_ip_ma[!is.na(rev_cntr), .(bene_id, daystart_dt, dayend_dt, 
                                                         icd_dgns_cd1, rev_cntr, crossover_rev = T)]),
                    by = c("bene_id", "daystart_dt", "dayend_dt", "icd_dgns_cd1", "rev_cntr"), 
                    all.x = T) %>%
  .[is.na(crossover_rev) , crossover_rev := F]



# create overall flag - true if rev is crossover and cpt is crossover or missing, OR
#                              cpt is crossover and rev is crossover or missing
# (necessary because some days have both rev and CPT)
all_ip_taf[ , crossover := (crossover_rev == T & (crossover_cpt == T | is.na(hcpcs_cd))) |
                           (crossover_cpt == T & (crossover_rev == T | is.na(rev_cntr)))] %>%
  .[ , c("crossover_rev", "crossover_cpt") := NULL]

# bind TAF and MA back together
all_ip <- rbind(all_ip_taf, 
                all_ip_ma[ , crossover := F])

# drop ip crossover claims
all_ip <- all_ip[crossover == F]
```


## Drop Residential crossover claims

```{r}
# merge TAF onto MA by date, diagnosis, and CPT
all_res_ma <- merge(all_res_ma,
                    unique(all_res_taf[!is.na(hcpcs_cd), .(bene_id, daystart_dt, dayend_dt, 
                                                           icd_dgns_cd1, hcpcs_cd, crossover_cpt = T)]),
                    by = c("bene_id", "daystart_dt", "dayend_dt", "icd_dgns_cd1", "hcpcs_cd"), 
                    all.x = T) %>%
  .[is.na(crossover_cpt) , crossover_cpt := F]


# merge TAF onto MA by date, diagnosis, and revenue code 
all_res_ma <- merge(all_res_ma,
                    unique(all_res_taf[!is.na(rev_cntr), .(bene_id,daystart_dt, dayend_dt, 
                                                           icd_dgns_cd1, rev_cntr, crossover_rev = T)]),
                    by = c("bene_id", "daystart_dt", "dayend_dt", "icd_dgns_cd1", "rev_cntr"), 
                    all.x = T) %>%
  .[is.na(crossover_rev) , crossover_rev := F]


# create overall flag
all_res_ma[ , crossover := (crossover_rev == T & (crossover_cpt == T | is.na(hcpcs_cd))) |
                           (crossover_cpt == T & (crossover_rev == T | is.na(rev_cntr)))] %>%
  .[ , c("crossover_rev", "crossover_cpt") := NULL]
 
# bind TAF and MA back together
all_res <- rbind(all_res_taf[ , crossover := F], 
                 all_res_ma)

# drop residential crossovers
all_res <- all_res[crossover == F]
```


## Recombine claims

```{r}
ipres_all <- rbind(all_ip, 
                   all_res)

rm(all_res, all_ip)
```


# Address overlapping IP/Res days

For single-day claims, we find it unlikely that someone would be discharged from the hospital, enter a residential facility and be discharged on the same day. For these claims we'll set the setting to inpatient.

For multi-day claims where at least 2 days of the encounter overlap we count the overlapping days as inpatient (single day overlaps are likely a same day transfer). 

```{r}
# group consecutive days with a visit_id
ipres_all <- ipres_all[order(bene_id, start_dt, end_dt)]
ipres_all[ , visit_id := chse::overlapping(start_dt, 
                                           end_dt, 
                                           maxgap = -2), by = bene_id]

# roll up values by visit_id
ipres_all[ , `:=` (visstart_dt = min(start_dt), 
                   visend_dt = max(end_dt), 
                   smi_dx = max(smi_dx), 
                   mmmi_dx = max(mmmi_dx), 
                   sud_dx = max(sud_dx),
                   ip = max(setting %in% "ip"), 
                   res = max(setting %in% "res")), by = .(bene_id, visit_id)] %>%
  .[ , days := as.numeric(visend_dt - visstart_dt + 1)] 


# if there are overlap settings, count as IP (the higher level of care)
ipres_all[ip == T & res == T, res := F]

# if there is a 1-day IP and a 1-day Res on the same day, these wouldn't have been caught but should be fixed. 

# make IP if any IP on the day
ipres_all[ , ip_new := max(ip), by = .(bene_id, visstart_dt, visend_dt)]

# adjust
ipres_all[ , ip := ip_new][ , "ip_new" := NULL]

# recreate setting var
ipres_all[ , setting := ifelse(ip == T, "ip", "res")]
```


# Assign diagnosis to visit  

Flag the visit as SUD if any SUD, then SMI if any SMI, then mild to moderate. 

```{r}
ipres_all[ , dx_cat := fcase(sud_dx == T, "sud",
                             smi_dx == T, "smi",
                             mmmi_dx == T, "mmmi")]
```


# Roll up to days

Roll up to TAF, MA, or both per setting/diagnosis/day.  

```{r}
# flag if day has both MA and TAF for the setting/dx
ipres_all[ , both := uniqueN(source) == 2, by = .(bene_id, daystart_dt, setting, dx_cat)]

# update source to both taf/ma
ipres_all[both == T, source := "tafma"]
```


# Sum days 

There should be at most 2 rows per bene-day, 1 for IP and 1 for Residential, on a transfer day.

```{r}
# make unique by day
ipres_days <- unique(ipres_all[ , .(bene_id, dx_cat, daystart_dt, 
                                    setting, source, year = year(daystart_dt))])

# sum visits by setting and diagnosis
ipres_days <- ipres_days[ , .(days = uniqueN(daystart_dt)), by = .(bene_id, year, setting, source, dx_cat)]

# create a column name combining source, setting, and dx_cat
ipres_days[ , varname := paste(setting, "days", dx_cat, source, sep = "_")]

# reshape to wide format
ipres_days <- dcast(ipres_days, bene_id + year ~ varname, value.var = "days", fill = 0) 
```
